official.deadline_note: The 2026 round opened 16 June 2026 and closed 11 September 2026; no 2027 window is published. Aurora states up to four scholarships will be awarded yearly from 2024 to 2026.
official.status_note: The Indigenous Pathways Portal lists the scholarship as Closed after the 11 September 2026 closing date; no 2027 dates are published.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The scholarship may be used for university fees/payment of HECS.
benefits: Up to AUD 120,000 per year for up to three years as a contribution towards the cost of full-time postgraduate study or research
Access to up to AUD 5,000 per year in tailored academic and wellbeing support
Scaffolded personal, social, academic and wellbeing support facilitated by Aurora, including an Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander support person
Community and network-building opportunities connecting scholars with one another and Aurora's Alumni network
No need to re-apply each year once awarded
eligibility: Be of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander descent, identify as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander and be accepted as such by the community in which you live or have lived
Provide written confirmation of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander identity from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council

Undertake full-time postgraduate study (graduate certificate, masters or PhD) or research in a cancer-related field in health, research or policy at a recognised university or institute in Australia, the US or UK
Be a graduate student, health professional or early-career researcher
Demonstrate how the study or research will impact Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities in improving cancer-related outcomes
Demonstrate an aspiration towards employment or continued employment in a cancer-related field
Provide a budget outlining how the scholarship funds will be used, also outlining all additional funding and income
requirements: Undertake full-time postgraduate study or research
Scholarship funds cannot be used for study or research expenses that should be covered by the university or institute
Applications are not considered complete and do not pass shortlisting if all required documents are not submitted by the closing date
documents: Personal statement of no more than two pages covering community identification and contributions, the course/research and key focus areas, community impact, skills and knowledge to be developed, and career aspiration
Written confirmation of full-time enrolment from the relevant university/institution, or written confirmation of application and/or research proposal submitted
High-resolution corporate headshot in jpeg format
Copy of the most up-to-date official academic transcript
Budget outlining how scholarship funds will be used (template within the application form)
Confirmation of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander identity through a signed statement from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council
One written reference from an Elder or a senior member of your community
Two written academic references, or one academic and one professional reference, for those undertaking graduate study or research
All references emailed by the referee directly to scholarships@aurorafoundation.com.au
selection_criteria: Ability to demonstrate how the study or research will impact Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities in improving cancer-related outcomes
Aspiration towards employment or continued employment in a cancer-related field
Shortlisting requires all required documents to be submitted by the scholarship closing date
coverage: Accommodation and/or travel expenses related to research, fieldwork or conferences
Textbooks and other essential study-related equipment
Living expenses (accommodation, transportation, food and other dietary requirements)
Access to academic, health and wellbeing services
application_method: Read the First Nations Cancer Scholarship Guidelines (linked PDF) to confirm eligibility criteria and required documents
Apply via Aurora's Indigenous Pathways Portal
Ensure referees email references directly to scholarships@aurorafoundation.com.au
Optionally contact the Aurora Pathways Scholarship team before applying to discuss the application
official.application_route: Apply through Aurora's Indigenous Pathways Portal with the full document set before the closing date
official.citizenship_residency: Open to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students only
official.international_eligibility: Study or research may be undertaken at recognised universities or institutes in Australia, the US or UK
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Cancer-related field in health, research or policy; published study areas include clinical and allied health fields (e.g. oncology, nursing, palliative care), policy fields (e.g. public health, health leadership and management) and research fields (e.g. laboratory and clinical research, social and cultural determinants of cancer)
official.research_requirement: Applicants must be undertaking full-time graduate study or research in a cancer-related field; research applicants provide written confirmation from a recognised research institute or a submitted research proposal
official.duration: Up to three years, with no need to re-apply each year once awarded
official.description: Established by the Aurora Education Foundation and Cancer Australia, and funded by the Australian Government through Cancer Australia, the First Nations Cancer Scholarship supports Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander graduate students, health professionals and early-career researchers to undertake full-time postgraduate study or research in a cancer-related field, valued at up to AUD 120,000 per year for up to three years.
official.program_type: Charitable foundation and government co-funded research scholarship (Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander graduate students)

verification.notes: Verified on Aurora's official programme page and the Indigenous Pathways Portal listing: up to AUD 120,000 per year for up to three years plus up to AUD 5,000 per year in tailored academic and wellbeing support, the eligible-use list, the eligibility and document lists, and the 2026 round dates (opened 16 June 2026, closed 11 September 2026, status Closed).

applicant_utility.summary: Worth up to AUD 120,000 a year for up to three years, plus up to AUD 5,000 a year in tailored academic and wellbeing support, and you do not re-apply each year once awarded - but it is only for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants, and you must show how your cancer-related study or research will improve outcomes for your communities. The document list is heavy: a two-page personal statement, a budget using Aurora's template, community identity confirmation from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council, an Elder's reference, academic or professional references, and even a corporate headshot, with referees emailing references directly to Aurora. The 2026 round closed on 11 September 2026 and no 2027 window is published yet, so watch the Indigenous Pathways Portal and contact the scholarships team early.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander graduate students, health professionals or early-career researchers committed to full-time cancer-control study, research or policy work.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you meet the identity criteria and can obtain written confirmation from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council
Read the Scholarship Guidelines PDF before drafting anything
Secure written confirmation of full-time enrolment, or of your submitted application and/or research proposal
Draft the two-page personal statement against Aurora's five required content points
Complete the budget template, including all other funding and income
Brief your referees early so they email references directly to scholarships@aurorafoundation.com.au before the deadline
Organise the corporate headshot, current CV and most recent official transcript in advance
common_rejection_risks: Missing documents, which Aurora states stop the application passing shortlisting
References not sent directly by the referee to Aurora
A personal statement that omits any required element, especially community impact and career aspiration
A budget that leaves out other income or funding sources
Failing to demonstrate impact on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities
Requesting funds for expenses the university or institute should cover
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any study or research-related expenses that should be covered by the university or institute, and any costs beyond the approved budget within the up-to-AUD 120,000 annual value
document_audit: The personal statement has a strict two-page limit and five required content points
Identity confirmation must come from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council, not from your own statement alone
References must arrive from the referee directly, so give referees weeks of notice
A high-resolution corporate headshot in jpeg format is a required document
The budget template sits inside the application form
alerts: The 2026 round closed on 11 September 2026 and the portal shows the scholarship as Closed with no 2027 dates published
Aurora states up to four scholarships are awarded yearly from 2024 to 2026, so continuation beyond 2026 is not confirmed by the awarding body
Study can be in Australia, the US or UK, but must be full time
Award holders do not re-apply each year, so a missed round can mean waiting for the next published window
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Read the guidelines, assemble the portal document set (personal statement, budget, transcript, CV, headshot, identity confirmation, and references emailed directly by referees), then submit through the Indigenous Pathways Portal before the closing date.
